2. **The Model2Vec fused lift shrinks as n grows**: +31% at n=13, +11% at n=16, +1.7% at n=882. The pattern says the small-repo gains were noise, and at power, Model2Vec semantic on history is parity — consistent with the original "M2V is noise on history prose" probe. The question the Gemma runs will answer is whether the stronger embedder changes that, which is exactly what its clean separation on the 2026-06-08 probe predicted it might.

One honest caveat on "fix ollama": the brew formula was genuinely broken (ships no llama-server runner), and the cask app's binary wedges in `_dyld_start` when launched headlessly — it likely needs one interactive GUI launch from your login session to clear first-run verification. Rather than stay blocked, I stood up the spike's documented runner instead: node-llama-cpp serving the canonical `ggml-org` GGUF (the artifact alignment.md explicitly prefers over the Ollama blob) on `:11500` at ~17ms/embed. Embedding capability is fully working; the Ollama app itself could use one manual launch from you at some point.

  for questions settled negatively.
- Ranking: factLexicalScore unifies the lexical arm (term score + locus
  boost + closed-negative boost) for rankFacts and the fused ranker, so the
  two paths cannot drift. The boost applies only to already-matching facts
  and no existing fact carries the kind, so measured baselines are unchanged

## Changes

- **`closed-negative` kind** added to the closed set, top of inference priority. `closedNegativeCues` (ruled out / measured as noise / dead end / tried and failed / revisit only if / …) checked before gotcha cues — a dead end phrased as a trap is still a dead end. **Phase 2, item 1 is shipped** — PR #23 merged with all CI green. The `closed-negative` fact kind now exists end to end:

- **Kind + inference**: `closed-negative` in the closed set at top inference priority, with high-precision cues ("ruled out", "measured as noise", "dead end", "tried and failed", "revisit only if"…) checked before gotcha cues — a dead end phrased as a trap is still a dead end. A few extra gotcha cues landed alongside, chipping at the known 1-in-948 underfire.
- **Distill prompt**: a sixth kind with text-shape guidance (tried / why it failed / revisit-when, in one statement) and a new always-capture trigger for rejected designs, failed experiments, and measured non-levers — flagged as "the highest-value capture of all."
- **Ranking**: a new shared `factLexicalScore` (term score + locus boost + closed-negative boost) used by both `rankFacts` and the fused ranker so they can't drift. The +30 boost only applies to facts that already match, and since no existing fact carries the kind, every measured baseline stays bit-identical until new distills produce closed-negatives.

One deliberate non-action: I did *not* run `facts reclassify --force` on your live brain — force-mode would also overwrite agent-emitted kinds with inferred ones across all 948 facts, which is your call to make. A plain `reclassify` (fills only missing/invalid kinds) is safe whenever.

**Interim Gemma results** (entire-cli still running, ~2h): podcasts Gemma-fused hit **2.108 useful/1k vs 1.554 bm25 (+36%)** — a real lift. But entire-brain came in at 0.978, *below* its own Model2Vec-fused (1.219) and barely above bm25 — at n=13/16 these swing wildly, which is exactly why the n=882 entire-cli run is the one that decides. Full three-repo table when it completes.

fails (missing brain/repo is silence, only flag misuse errors), token-

Stopping here, as promised — I've hit a genuine decision point. Here's where things stand and the question.

## Shipped since "keep going" (all merged, CI green)

- **PR #23 — closed-negative fact kind** (Phase 2, item 1): the sixth kind with inference cues, distill-prompt hunting for settled-negative questions, and a ranking boost via a new shared `factLexicalScore`.
- **PR #24 — agent-harness hooks** (item 2): `hook pre-edit` (locus-anchored facts for the file being edited) and `hook post-failure` (gotcha/closed-negative matching on failure text), with a test-enforced harness-safety contract: silent empties, never fails, token-budgeted, warm-path only. Live smoke: pre-edit on `semantic.go` surfaces two real facts; everything else stays silent.
- **PR #25 — `brief --handoff`** (item 3): the session-resumption packet — last N distinct sessions with opening request and end-state decisions/validations, recent facts, and the sessions-since-distill blind-spot line. Live smoke on this repo's brain produces a genuinely readable trajectory (after fixing three data-quality issues the smoke test exposed: cross-branch session duplicates, tool-call JSON leaking into summaries, wrapper-injected requests).

## The Gemma verdict (recorded in the eval ledger)

| repo | n | substring | bm25 | fused-M2V | fused-Gemma |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| podcasts | 16 | 1.128 | 1.554 | 1.731 | **2.108** |
| entire-brain | 13 | 0.315 | 0.927 | 1.219 | 0.978 |
| entire-cli | **882** | 0.283 | 1.016 | 1.033 | **1.158** |

At real statistical power: Model2Vec-fused is **parity** with BM25 (the small-repo +31% was noise — the original "M2V is noise on history" probe was right), but **Gemma-fused is +14% with p=0.00075** (329W/248L on 577 informative pairs) — the same +14% the facts layer measured. The history semantic arm is now *validated, but only with the transformer embedder*.

## The question

That result creates a fork in priorities, and it's yours to call:

**Option A — productionize the Gemma-fused history arm now.** The measurement justifies it, but it's real work: query-time fusion over 267k records requires *persistent* history vectors (a one-time ~1.3h embed per big repo, then incremental on refresh), which means building the history vector store — naturally as vec0 under `brain_cgo`, looping back to Stage 1b — plus gating on a configured/reachable Gemma embedder, which today means a running local server.

**Option B — continue down Phase 2 in order**: item 4 (fact staleness/locus-drift signal) and item 5 (per-session incremental distill), which are pure agent-utility wins with no embedder-infrastructure dependency, and leave the history arm as a recorded, justified backlog item.

My lean is B — the Phase 2 items compound the delivery story you just started shipping, while A's value is capped until the in-process embedder lands anyway (a server dependency makes it opt-in-only either way). But A is the freshest validated win, and if the Librarian convergence is heating up, building the history vector store now front-loads shared-store work. Which way?

## Changes

- **`distill --session <id>`** — the bounded single-session path. Filtered sessions carry their cache entries through exactly like the `--branch` filter, so the next unfiltered run doesn't re-distill everything. `--session` + `--force` is rejected up front: force drops every distilled fact on the loaded branch but a session filter would re-derive only one session's — silent loss for the rest.
- **`hook session-end`** — deterministic refresh (agent=none, zero tokens) exports the just-ended session, then a distill bounded to it; proposals flow through the existing reconcile/review pipeline unchanged. Hook contract: empty stdout (summary to stderr), environment problems are silence. Unlike the warm-path hooks, this one may take minutes and spend tokens — the session is over, nobody is waiting. Re-fires are free via the incremental cache.

Session-filter semantics (only the named session costs agent calls; other sessions' cache entries survive even when their transcripts changed), the force-guard, and the existing hook-contract suite. Full suite green on both stacks.

content.text:
Found it — three compounding causes, one dominant. Here's the full diagnosis.

## Why the entire.io distill is crawling

**The dominant cause: the installed plugin binary is from Jun 7 — it predates the opencode-document stripping fix (PR #20, merged yesterday morning) — and entire.io is 75% opencode sessions.**

The numbers:
- **1,991 of 2,640 sessions (75%) are document-form transcripts** (opencode-style pretty-printed JSON), totaling **4.36 GB of the 5.63 GB corpus**, with files up to 52 MB.
- The Jun 7 binary's line-oriented preprocessor can't strip these — every line of an indented JSON document fails to parse individually — so they pass through **unstripped**: megabytes of tool output, diffs, and token accounting get chunked at 48 KB and fed to the agent. This is precisely the failure PR #20 fixed ("a 22.6 MB opencode session was 1.3% conversation text; the no-op strip cost ~75× the agent calls it should have").
- Unstripped, the document sessions alone are **~87,700 agent calls**. Stripped properly they'd be ~2–4 thousand.
- Each call spawns a fresh `claude --print` CLI process (Node boot + API round trip, no `--effort low` set either). Observed throughput: 881 sessions in 11h45m ≈ 48s/session — and the worst document sessions are mostly still ahead of the cursor. At this pace the remaining 1,759 sessions are **days**, not hours.

**Secondary findings:**
- **Concurrency isn't helping.** The binary has `--concurrency` (default 4), but the prefetch pool parallelizes chunks *within one session* — sessions are processed sequentially. I observed exactly one live `claude` child. For a corpus where stripped sessions are 1–2 chunks, cross-session parallelism is the lever that doesn't exist yet. That's a real architecture gap worth a backlog entry.
- **The Jun 7 binary also predates the pi-format routing fix** (`f02cd7f`), so any pi-style sessions distill to zero kept text, and it predates the closed-negative prompt — meaning the facts being produced are also lower-quality than what current main would extract. Some facts already written from raw-JSON chunks are likely junk-prone.

## Recommendation

Stop the run and restart on a current binary — the work isn't lost, and the broken sessions *should* be redone:

1. Kill the distill (pids 11801/11803).
2. Rebuild from main and replace `~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin/entire-brain` (single static binary).
3. Restart: `entire brain distill --agent claude-code --model claude-haiku-4-5 --effort low`.

The incremental cache makes this surgical: fingerprints hash the *preprocessed* text, so the 649 JSONL sessions already distilled keep matching and are skipped, while document-form and pi sessions' fingerprints invalidate — exactly the ones that were being distilled as garbage — and they re-distill properly at 1–3 calls each instead of hundreds. Ballpark for the full corpus on the new binary: ~3–5k agent calls ≈ **5–10 hours** instead of days, with meaningfully better facts (current prompt, real conversation text).

Want me to do the kill/rebuild/restart? I didn't touch the running process — 11¾ hours of someone's run isn't mine to kill on a diagnosis question.

lookahead held ~0.2 work-sessions, so the producer never reached the next
session with real agent work before the consumer blocked.

structs) while a separate work-lookahead semaphore bounds the sessions
holding preprocessed chunk text — acquired before the transcript read,
released by the consumer when the session's chunks are fully consumed — so
memory stays bounded to ~concurrency sessions' chunks while skip streaks
flow through freely.

content.text:
The distill is now properly fast. PR #31 is merged (all CI green) and the live run is at 154/2640 after ~10 minutes. Here's what it took — three bottlenecks, each found by watching the live run, fixed, and verified live:

**1. Per-session call pool → cross-session pipeline.** The original prefetcher parallelized chunks *within* one session, but a stripped session is 1–2 chunks (the corpus median), so `--concurrency 8` ran ~1 call at a time. The fix is a producer/consumer pipeline sharing one call pool across sessions, with results applied strictly in chronological order so reconcile and fact application keep their serial semantics. One subtlety mattered: dispatch must happen from a *single* dispatcher in global consumption order — per-session dispatchers over a shared semaphore can hand a freed slot to a session the consumer isn't ready for, which deadlocks at small pool sizes.

**2. Lookahead counted sessions, not work.** First live restart still showed one call in flight: resuming past 881 cached sessions means ~95% skips, and a 4-session lookahead held ~0.2 work-sessions. Now the session buffer is deep (skips are near-free structs) while a separate work-lookahead semaphore bounds memory to ~`concurrency` sessions' chunk text.

**3. Serial preprocessing starved the pool.** Second restart: 2 of 8 slots used — parsing a multi-MB document costs seconds, and the single producer couldn't prep sessions as fast as the pool retired calls. Prep now runs in parallel workers (bounded by the same work semaphore), with delivery and dispatch still in order.

**Result, measured live:** the pool saturates at 8 and the run moves at ~15–23 sessions/min in the mixed region, versus **1.25/min** on the old binary — and that's with `--effort low` and `--max-chunk-bytes 131072` (fewer, bigger calls) also in effect. Honest ETA for the full 2,640: **roughly 2–4 hours**, since the uncached tail is all real work. Everything is race-clean and the full suite passes on both stacks; the existing semantics (consumption-bounded abort, lazy sequential `concurrency<=1`, flush cadence, cache rules) carry over with their tests.

One known serial element remains if you ever want more: reconcile calls run inline in the consumer (order-dependent by design), so fact-rich stretches still serialize on them. Worth touching only if the current run's tail proves slow.

The run is going in the background (`/tmp/entireio-distill3.log`); when it completes, the entire.io capstone validation (Phase 2 item 9) unblocks — the four-arm history eval on a fourth, TypeScript-domain repo. The interrupted entire-cli midtask measurement is also still queued; I'll pick both up as they're ready.

**Reopening discipline (worked example, 2026-06-10):** scan-cache v3 closed

handoff packet and midtask mining became new consumers — new evidence — so v4
reopened it *narrowly*: requests are extracted again for trajectory surfaces

them from general ranking). Closed negatives are reopened by new consumers or
new measurements, never by forgetting why they closed.

- **Scoped-floor (recall floor via backfill facts):** dead end; backfill facts

content.text:
Found it — it's a small rendering inconsistency in the progress reporter, `internal/cli/progress.go`. Here's the mechanics:

You ran on a TTY, so the progress reporter is in **spinner mode**. In that mode, each step renders an in-place spinner while running, and when it finishes it clears the line and prints the `+` form — that's `Finish()`:

```go
if t.progress.spinner {
    fmt.Fprintf(t.progress.out, "%s+ %s done\n", clearTerminalLine, t.label)   // "+ … done"
}
fmt.Fprintf(t.progress.out, "%s: %s done\n", t.progress.prefix, t.label)      // non-TTY: "refresh: … done"
```

But your seed step didn't *finish* — it was **skipped** (the line ends in "skipped", not "done": a seed already existed and the deterministic refresh had nothing to redo). Skips go through a different method, `Skip()`, and that one only ever got the non-TTY rendering:

```go
func (p *refreshProgress) Skip(label string) {
    fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "%s: %s skipped\n", p.prefix, label)   // always "refresh: …", even on a TTY
}
```

So completed steps print `+ … done`, failures print `! … failed`, but skipped steps unconditionally print the `refresh: … skipped` form — the prefix style that's meant for non-TTY/log output. That's why your third line looks different: not a different step semantically, just a code path that never learned about spinner mode. It's purely cosmetic — the skip itself is correct behavior.

It's a five-line fix to make `Skip` TTY-aware with its own marker (e.g. `- seed baseline: … skipped`), consistent with `+`/`!`. Want me to fix it? I'd fold it into the next small PR rather than a dedicated one — or do it now if it bugs you.

# PR #33 review — DOCS + BENCHMARK ARTIFACTS slice

## Findings

### 1. MAJOR — Answer-bearing `brain_queries` are injected into the brain-arm prompts of all three suites the PR promotes to "citable release proof"
**Files:** `benchmarks/agent-brain/run.py` (`prompt_for`, ~line 2077), `benchmarks/agent-brain/tasks/entire-brain-history-codex-schema-contract.json`, `tasks/entireio-cli-manual-commit-attribution-base.json`, `tasks/entireio-cli-radar-manual-attribution-deletions.json`, claims in `docs/release_readiness_audit.md` and `docs/release_press_release.md`.

Every brain/MCP condition prompt embeds `Useful query terms: {brain_queries}` (or "these failing terms: `{queries}`"); the `no_brain` arm gets none. Spot-checks of the three retained "proof" suites:

- **Schema-contract suite** (66.0→91.5, 0/4→4/4): hidden validation requires the literal string `should rely on prompt plus local validation, not --output-schema` in the test file, and another check requires removing `--output-schema`. The brain-arm prompt's query terms include `"--output-schema"` and the near-verbatim fragment `"should rely on prompt plus local validation"`. A brain-arm agent can satisfy the hidden exact-string gate by echoing its prompt, without the brain.
- **MCP manual-attribution and Radar-deletions suites** (1/4→4/4 and 2/4→4/4): the fix is re-adding `state.RealignAttributionBase(newHead)`; brain_queries handed to the brain arm include `"RealignAttributionBase newHead manual commit hooks"` and `"BaseCommit AttributionBaseCommit realign"` — the fix's exact identifier and argument.
- The audit doc explicitly claims the manual-attribution panel works "without handing over hidden validation or expected text" — contradicted by the task file.
- The new task `entire-brain-semantic-tokenized-idf-ranking.json` has the same built-in leak (`tokenIDFWeight`, hidden test name `TestTokenizedSearchRanksRareTokenAboveCommonTokens` appear in brain_queries while validation requires `weights[i] = tokenIDFWeight(total, df)` verbatim).

The mechanism pre-exists on main (10 occurrences of "Useful query terms"), and the PR's leak auditor checks transcripts for harness markers/host paths — it never checks brain_queries overlap with hidden validation strings or the regressed identifier. The quoted numbers are real, but they measure *hint + brain* vs *no hint, no brain*. "Citable evidence that the brain improves the task" is overstated; at minimum the audit/press-release docs should disclose the query-term asymmetry as a confound, and the per-suite "without handing over expected text" sentence is wrong as written.

### 2. CLAIMS vs EVIDENCE — five claims traced; numbers all check out (no fabrication found)
- **Schema-contract**: `evidence/release/release-candidate-entire-brain-schema-contract-20260610T0115Z/summary.json` matches the doc exactly (mean 66.0→91.5, pass 0.0→1.0, `proof_ready=true`, `brain_positive_stable`, 8 records, 8/8 provenance). Doc honestly notes the token/time overhead.
- **Radar deletions**: I recomputed means from the 8 individual `record.json` files — scores (94+50+54+94)/4=73.0 and (93+93+93+91)/4=92.5, tokens 811,466.5→408,947.75, search calls 11.5→6.0 all match the doc to the decimal. Records have distinct timestamps, token counts, and one genuine 835-second failed no-brain run; `mcp-server.log` carries the claimed `tool: brain_regressions` / `tool_result: ... ok` lines. No copy-paste/fabrication signals.
- **MCP manual-attribution**: summary matches (0.25→1.0 pass, 76.25→92.0); its server logs are indeed count-only legacy logs and the doc correctly downgrades it to "not named-tool proof, not efficiency proof".
- **Distill perf**: `evidence/distill-perf/dry-run.json` = 147 sessions / 7,419,024 bytes / 159 chunks / 159 calls as quoted; jobs-1 18.28s vs jobs-4 9.16s = 1.996x ("about 2x" ✓, manifest `min_speedup` 1.25); manifest claim_scope is properly narrow ("current-repo local command-agent ... not model quality"). Note the "agent" is a deterministic local fake (~76ms/call) — the doc discloses this.
- **Workspace-radar no-claim** and **codex-audit totals** (3 suites, 24 records, 0 hard flags, 8 MCP-verified, 4 named-tool verified/completed; no-brain 89 vs early-stop 85) all match committed artifacts.

### 3. MINOR — Stale/internally inconsistent numbers in `docs/release_readiness_audit.md`
- Line 528 says the radar-tool artifact covers "**51** focused `internal/cli` tests"; line 606 and the committed `evidence/radar-tool/manifest.json` say **52** (the jsonl has 52 passing top-level tests). 51 is wrong.
- Line ~262: "The independent release audit retained under `benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/release` reports **1 suite, 8 records** ... and 1 proof-ready comparison" — the committed `codex-audit-report.json` now reports 3 suites / 24 records / 3 proof-ready comparisons. Stale sentence from an earlier pass.

### 4. MINOR — Numbers quoted with no committed artifact
The audit doc quotes precise non-retained results: semantic refresh counts (134 files / 2,250 symbols / 14,883 relations at `721aae0`; 137 / 2,405 / 17,091 at `b430963`) and the facts smoke (39,242 history records, raw-sessions 42,124.75 tokens / 0.0148 useful-per-1k, history 921.25 / 1.0342). They are hedged as local/non-retained and "not release proof", but they're unverifiable from the repo; consider either retaining artifacts or rounding/dropping the false-precision decimals.

### 5. MINOR — Record-vs-log MCP call-count mismatch the auditor doesn't catch
In `release-candidate-cli-radar-mcp-del-20260610-r2`, every `mcp_history` `record.json` reports `mcp_tool_calls: 2` with two identical `brain_regressions` detail entries, while the corresponding `mcp-server.log` shows exactly **one** `tools/call` / one `tool: brain_regressions`. Looks like client-side double-counting; the prompt mandates "EXACTLY ONCE" and the cross-checking auditor passes it anyway. Doesn't change verdicts, but the "auditor cross-checks summaries against record rows" story misses this.

### 6. Consistency with main — clean
- `docs/eval_ledger.md`: untouched (0-line diff). No PR doc contradicts ledger entries; nothing in the new docs claims Model2Vec/Gemma/BM25 numbers, and the README's "facts + BM25 history/docs" search description is consistent with the ledger's "history BM25 default, facts BM25 opt-in".
- `docs/semantic_brain_plan.md`: Phase 2 "Agent Utility" (items 1–9) is byte-identical to main; the PR's edits are confined to Phase-1 command renames (`index` → `refresh index`, `context` → `inspect context`, etc.). One cosmetic bug: the edit leaves `entire brain inspect boundaries --kind route|tool|workflow --json` **duplicated** in the command block (~lines 159/164).
- `panels/full.json`: only *adds* a task; no gate weakening. New `release-*` panels and the release `manifest.json` raise requirements (4 reps/side, named-tool scopes, per-suite proof-ready) rather than lower them.
- `docs/durable_facts_plan.md` and `README.md` edits are honest claim-narrowing (signed→retained anchors, explicit egress caveats) — good changes.

### 7. Press release (`docs/release_press_release.md`) — mostly disciplined
Heavily hedged; every number it cites (1/4→4/4, 2/4→4/4) traces to committed artifacts, and it carries explicit "do not claim yet" sections. Two nits: "one retained replay-lab history proof where `full_brain` improved the task score/pass-rate" and the two MCP "proofs" inherit the Finding-1 confound and should disclose the query-hint asymmetry; "workspace-radar MCP harnessing" under "Shipped" is fine since outcome proof is separately listed as pending.

## Bottom line
No fabricated artifacts and the arithmetic is faithfully transcribed — the evidence chain (summary → records → logs → independent audit report) is real and self-consistent. The one substantive problem is Finding 1: the brain-arm prompts of all three suites the PR graduates to "citable proof" contain answer-bearing query terms (in one case a near-verbatim fragment of the hidden validation string), which the PR's otherwise elaborate leak/claim-hygiene machinery does not detect, and which directly contradicts the audit doc's "without handing over hidden validation or expected text" sentence. I'd treat that as must-fix wording (disclose the confound, or stop calling these "proof") before merge; findings 3–5 are quick text/artifact touch-ups.

Both changes are individually defensible (salt correctness; stable collision-free dirs — the old collision numbering genuinely depended on the branch set), but the cost is undocumented and the fallback is fake.

**5. MINOR — successful agent runs now fail on chatty stderr.**
`distill_cmd.go:1701-1710`: stderr is newly capped at 256KB and `stderr.Exceeded()` returns an error *even when the command exited 0* (previously stderr was unbounded and ignored on success). Also the `Exceeded` checks precede the `err != nil` check, so a failing-and-chatty agent yields the less useful "stderr exceeds N bytes" instead of the agent's real error. (The capped buffer itself is a good fix — the old code buffered unbounded output then checked size.)

**6. MINOR — new distill evidence fields are wiped by facts admin commands.**
`facts_manifest.go:91-105` `preserveFactDistillEvidence` preserves only CacheHits/FailedChunks/PreprocessedBytes/3-of-4 timings/Warnings; `Agent`, `Model`, `Effort`, `Jobs`, `EffectiveJobs`, `MaxChunkBytes`, `Confidence`, `ExtractionCalls`, `ReconcileCalls`, `TotalAgentCalls`, `TotalSeconds`, `Branch`, `Force` get zeroed by any `facts review/promote/gc` (`summarizeFactSource` rebuilds the source). Release-evidence audits reading these manifest fields will see them blanked.

**7. MINOR — timing/parallelism metrics don't measure what their names claim.**
`distill_cmd.go:862-864`: `extractionSeconds` measures consumer *wait* time on the prefetched result channel — with `--concurrency > 1`, calls that completed in the background register ~0s, so `extraction_seconds` undercounts. `EffectiveJobs` (:1130) is just `min(requested, calls)`, not observed parallelism, despite the `effective_extraction_jobs` name. **8. MINOR — dead code in the dry-run plan.**
`distillChunkWork` (:393-400) carries `Anchor`, `Chunk`, `Session`, `SessionIndex`, `ChunkIndex` that are never read (only `len(plan.Work)` is used); `distillPlan.Manifest`/`PrevCache` are stored and unused; `resolveDistillBranch` (:984) duplicates the `resolveBranch` closure in `runDistillForBrain` (:665) — drift risk. Similarly `var urlpkgParse = url.Parse` (`embed_ollama.go:190`) is a test seam never overridden by any test.

**9. MINOR — history branch annotation fallback yields mangled branch names.**
`history.go:363-384` `historyRecordBranchForPath` falls back to parsing the directory component, but with the new naming that's `<slug>-<sha8>` (e.g. `a-b-1f2e3d4c`) or the slugged default branch (`release-2024` for `release/2024`) — not real branch names. Only hits sessions absent from the manifest map, but it stores wrong `Branch` values in the index rather than leaving them empty.

**10. MINOR — inconsistent path guards.**
`export.go` `writeTranscriptFile`/`reuseTranscriptFromCursor` reject `"."` and `"../"`-prefixed paths but not bare `".."`, unlike `readBrainRelativeFile` (`distill_cmd.go:1644`) and `cleanBrainRelativePath` (`brain.go:243`).   ```

content.text:
Review done — three agents covered the distill/core slice, the eval/MCP/new-commands slice, and the docs/benchmark-evidence slice, building and reproducing findings on the branch. Here's my verdict.

## PR #33 review: Request changes — 3 blockers, 2 must-fix disclosures

**First, the good news.** This is a serious, mostly honest piece of work: today's cross-session distill pipeline survives intact (the PR builds on it correctly — cache salting, perf counters, dry-run, write-lock wrapping are layered on top, no races found); there are **no network-egress violations** (the new `--agent ollama` runner is loopback-enforced); **no closed negatives are re-litigated**; and the benchmark evidence chain is **not fabricated** — we recomputed means from individual record files and every quoted number traces to committed artifacts, to the decimal. The README/durable-facts doc edits are honest claim-*narrowing*.

### Blockers

1. **The history-eval pipeline is broken end-to-end.** New `validateEvalTask` requires `label_source` on labeled tasks, but `history_eval.go` (untouched) never emits it — reproduced with the built binary: `history-eval-gen` output is rejected by `history-eval`, as is **every pre-existing task file on disk**, including the sets behind this week's ledger rows. Same root cause breaks blocker #2: `facts eval-compare` now hard-errors on history summaries, contradicting the still-shipped help text ("works on the summaries unchanged"). One fix covers both: emit the new relevance metadata from the history arm, or grandfather empty sources as proxy rows.
2. **Confirmed nil-pointer panic in retrieval.** The new loopback guard makes `newOllamaEmbedder()` return nil, but `configuredEmbedder` immediately calls methods on it — so in the *exact scenario the hardening targets* (non-loopback `ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBED_URL`), every `search`/`vsearch`/`query` crashes instead of falling back to Model2Vec. Reproduced in a test.
3. **The export write-lock holds the exclusive brain lock for minutes while everyone else times out at 10s** — a concurrent distill's *final* flush errors out, failing an hours-long run at its last step. Worse, `openHistoryFTS` now takes the **write** lock on the query read path, serializing all concurrent searches.

### Must-fix disclosures (not code)

4. **The flagship "proof" suites have an answer-leak confound.** All three suites the audit graduates to citable proof inject answer-bearing `brain_queries` into the brain-arm prompts only — in one case a near-verbatim fragment of the hidden validation string, in two others the fix's exact identifier (`RealignAttributionBase`). The numbers are real, but they measure *hint+brain vs no-hint*, and the audit's sentence "without handing over hidden validation or expected text" is factually wrong as written. The PR's elaborate leak auditor never checks this vector. Disclose the confound or stop calling these proof.
5. **Silent full re-distill on upgrade.** The cache salt plus branch-directory renaming invalidates *every* fingerprint, and the "legacy migration" fallback is dead code that can never match — first run after merge re-distills the world. Directly relevant right now: it would invalidate the entire.io cache we're 2,338/2640 sessions into building (≈4,000 facts, ~14h of compute across runs). The cost may be justified; it must be documented, and the fake fallback removed.

### Also worth fixing (selected from ~15 minors)

`distill --dry-run` predicts wrongly under the default `--agent auto` (salt hashes "auto", real runs hash the resolved agent) and has zero tests despite shipping as release evidence; `brain status` now runs uncapped fact verification — hundreds of git subprocesses on a hot path; successful agent runs newly fail on >256KB stderr; the distill evidence fields get wiped by `facts review/promote/gc`; `--strict`/`--fail-on-unverifiable` bind the same bool; stale numbers in the audit doc (51 vs 52 tests; 1-suite vs 3-suite audit sentence); a duplicated command line in the plan doc.

**Recommendation:** the architecture and evidence discipline are worth merging *after* the two eval blockers, the panic, and the lock scoping are fixed, with the confound disclosed and the upgrade cost documented — ideally timed so the entire.io/entire-brain caches get one cycle on the current fingerprints first. Want me to post this as a formal GitHub review on the PR (I'd structure it as the blockers inline + a summary comment), or hand it back to you to deliver?

content.text:
All three blockers are fixed, tested, and pushed to the PR branch (`15e7aaa`, 9 files, +229/−35). Verified end-to-end with the built binary: `history-eval-gen → history-eval → eval-compare` works again (with `release_claimable: false` and proxy evidence basis correctly preserved — the claim discipline survives), legacy task files load, the non-loopback embed URL falls back to Model2Vec instead of panicking, and the full branch suite is green.

The one design subtlety worth knowing: the PR's own tests caught me over-correcting. My first compare fix allowed any same-source pair; but `source_match` relevance is computed from *each arm's own surfaced set* — side-dependent truth — so the PR is right to gate it. The landed rule: **same task-fixed ground truth** (explicit labels, same source) compares by default; **proof grade** (human/judge) exclusively gates claimability; side-dependent truths still require `--allow-proxy-comparison`.

## The alternative for #5 (silent full re-distill on upgrade)

The problem: salting fingerprints with agent/model/taxonomy *and* renaming branch dirs invalidates every existing cache entry — the first post-merge run re-distills the world (for entire.io, that's the ~14 hours of compute we just spent, again), and the PR's "legacy fallback" can never match by construction.

**Recommended: lazy grandfathering (dual-read cache).** ~60–80 lines, all in the cache layer:

1. Keep the *old* fingerprint function genuinely computable (no salt, old key format, old path layout — the legacy slug is derivable by stripping the new `-sha8` suffix).
2. On a new-format cache miss, compute the legacy fingerprint against the legacy key; on a match, accept it as cached and **rewrite under the new key** — zero agent calls. Entries migrate lazily on first touch; the legacy read path can be deleted a release later.
3. **Stop hashing the transcript path into the fingerprint at all.** Identity is SessionID + content hash; the path is storage layout, and hashing it guarantees that *any* future layout change re-invalidates the world again. This makes the branch-dir rename free now and forever.
4. Semantics are honest: grandfathered entries reflect whatever agent produced them — exactly pre-PR behavior, so no regression — while the salt governs all *new* entries, so `--model` changes invalidate correctly going forward. If strictness is wanted, add an explicit `--invalidate-cache` flag rather than imposing it silently.
5. Test: fixture cache in the old format → run new binary → assert zero agent calls and a rewritten cache.

Two simpler-but-worse options for completeness: a one-shot `brain migrate-cache` command (explicit, but nobody will know to run it before the expensive surprise), or abort-with-warning unless `--accept-full-redistill` (safe but hostile). The lazy dual-read gives correct behavior with zero user action.

Still open for the author (judgment calls, not code): the benchmark **confound disclosure** — the three "proof" suites feed answer-bearing query hints to the brain arm only, and the audit doc's "without handing over expected text" sentence is wrong as written — plus the minor doc/number cleanups from the review. Want me to post the full review + fix summary as a comment on PR #33 so suhaanthayyil has the context, and should I go ahead and implement the lazy-grandfathering cache as a follow-up commit on the branch?

# Release Blockers

A register of release-gating findings from the PR #33 review (2026-06-11),
kept next to the audit so a release decision can see what is open, what was
fixed, and exactly why. The standard for this file is the eval ledger's:
explicit claims, exact evidence, no euphemism.

## OPEN — B1: Answer-bearing query hints confound every "citable proof" suite

**The claim under audit.** `docs/release_readiness_audit.md` graduates three
benchmark suites to citable release proof and asserts the panels work
"without handing over hidden validation or expected text". **That sentence is
false as written**, for all three suites and for at least one newer task.

**The mechanism.** `benchmarks/agent-brain/run.py` (`prompt_for`) injects
`Useful query terms: {brain_queries}` into the **brain/MCP-arm prompts only**;
the `no_brain` arm receives no such terms. Whatever appears in a task's
`brain_queries` is therefore handed to exactly the arm whose superiority the
suite is supposed to prove. The committed task files put answer-bearing
content there:

| Suite (claimed result) | What `brain_queries` hands the brain arm | What the hidden validation requires |
|---|---|---|
| `entire-brain-history-codex-schema-contract` (score 66.0→91.5, pass 0/4→4/4) | The literal strings `"should rely on prompt plus local validation"` and ``"Checkpoint-context review reverted Codex `--output-schema` usage"`` | `rg 'should rely on prompt plus local validation, not --output-schema' internal/cli/seed_test.go` finds ≥1 match, and `--output-schema` is removed from `seed.go` — i.e. the prompt contains, near-verbatim, the exact string a hidden check greps for. An agent can pass by echoing its own prompt into a comment. |
| `entireio-cli-manual-commit-attribution-base` (pass 1/4→4/4, score 76.25→92.0) | `"RealignAttributionBase newHead manual commit hooks"`, `"BaseCommit AttributionBaseCommit realign"`, and the hidden-adjacent test name `"TestManualCommit_AttributionStaleBase"` | Hidden tests pass only when the fix re-adds the call `state.RealignAttributionBase(newHead)` — **the exact function name and argument are in the brain arm's prompt**. |
| `entireio-cli-radar-manual-attribution-deletions` (pass 2/4→4/4, score 73.0→92.5) | Identical `brain_queries` to the row above | Same hidden tests; same leak. |
| `entire-brain-semantic-tokenized-idf-ranking` (newer, not yet promoted) | `"tokenIDFWeight rare token ranking"` and the **hidden test's exact name** `"TestTokenizedSearchRanksRareTokenAboveCommonTokens"` | `rg 'weights\[i\] = tokenIDFWeight\(total, df\)'` finds exactly one match — the prompt names the function the hidden grep requires verbatim. |

**Why this is a confound and not a nitpick.** The suites measure
*(answer-bearing hint + brain)* versus *(no hint, no brain)*. Any observed
lift decomposes into (a) the hint telling the agent what the fix is and (b)
the brain retrieving context — and the committed artifacts cannot separate
them. In the schema-contract case the hint alone is sufficient to pass the
hidden exact-string gate with zero retrieval. The numbers themselves are
real (recomputed from the per-record artifacts during review; timestamps,
token counts, and logs are consistent and one genuine no-brain failure run is
retained) — what is unsupported is the *attribution* of the lift to the
brain.

**Why the PR's own hygiene machinery missed it.** The leak auditor checks
*transcripts* for harness markers and host paths; it never intersects
`brain_queries` with hidden-validation command strings, expected-text greps,
or hidden test names. The `Useful query terms` mechanism predates this PR
(present on `main` in 10 tasks), so prior comparisons carry the same
confound; this PR is gated on it because it is the one promoting these suites
to "citable proof".

**Required to clear B1 (all of):**

1. Strip answer-bearing terms from `brain_queries` in the affected tasks — no
   identifiers from the expected fix, no substrings of hidden-validation
   greps, no hidden test names — or give both arms identical hints so the
   delta isolates retrieval.
2. Extend the leak auditor: flag any `brain_queries` token (or ≥3-word
   substring) that appears in hidden validation commands, expected strings,
   or hidden test names. The four rows above must fail the auditor as it
   stands.
3. Re-run the three suites clean and re-promote only what survives.
4. Until then, correct the audit sentence and the two press-release "proof"
   bullets to disclose the confound explicitly.

## RESOLVED — fixed during review on this branch

**R1 — Eval label discipline orphaned the history-eval pipeline** (fixed in
`15e7aaa`). `validateEvalTask` rejected `history-eval-gen` output and every
retained task file; `eval-compare` hard-errored on its own default eval-gen
output. Fix separates ground-*truth* (same explicit labels, same source →
comparable) from evidence *grade* (human/judge-refined → claimable);
history-eval now declares `provenance_silver`, legacy files default to it,
and side-dependent truths (`source_match`, runtime judge) stay gated behind
`--allow-proxy-comparison`. Covered by a new gen→load→run→compare seam test.

**R2 — Retrieval panic on the loopback guard's own rejection path** (fixed in
`15e7aaa`). `configuredEmbedder` dereferenced the nil returned for a
non-loopback `ENTIRE_BRAIN_EMBED_URL`; every `search`/`vsearch`/`query`
crashed in the exact scenario the guard hardens. Now degrades to the bundled
Model2Vec embedder with a warning; regression test added.

**R3 — Brain write-lock scoping** (fixed in `15e7aaa`). Export held the
exclusive lock across the minutes-long transcript phase while every other
user times out at 10s — failing a concurrent distill's FINAL flush (an
hours-long run killed at its last step) — and `openHistoryFTS` took the write
lock on the query READ path, serializing all searches. Export now locks only
the shared-artifact phases; FTS opens fresh indexes lock-free and
double-checks freshness under the lock only for rebuilds.

**R4 — Silent full re-distill on upgrade** (fixed alongside this file). The
fingerprint salt plus the stable-branch-dir rename invalidated every existing
cache entry, and the shipped "legacy key" fallback could never match (a
legacy-format fingerprint never equals a salted one) — the first post-upgrade
run would re-distill the entire corpus (observed scale: ~14h of agent calls
for a 2,640-session brain). Fixed with lazy grandfathering: the legacy
formula is kept genuinely computable (including pre-rename transcript paths),
a matching legacy entry counts as cached and is rewritten under the new
key/format on first touch, and the transcript path is no longer hashed into
the new fingerprint at all — storage layout is not identity, and hashing it
re-invalidates the world on every future layout change. The filtered-session
carry-through, which copied legacy-format fingerprints under new-format keys
(making them permanently unmatchable), now preserves entries under their own
keys. Covered by `TestDistillCacheGrandfathersLegacyEntries`, including the
renamed-branch-dir case and the changed-content negative.

Done — both deliverables are on PR #33 (`15e7aaa` + `90e061e`), full branch suite green.

**The lazy cache grandfathering** (commit `90e061e`) implements the design end to end:

- The legacy fingerprint formula is now *genuinely* computable — pathful, unsalted, exactly as main wrote it — with pre-rename transcript-path candidates derived by stripping the new `-<sha8>` branch-dir suffix. A matching legacy entry counts as cached and is rewritten under the new key/format on first touch: lazy migration, zero agent calls.
- The transcript path is no longer hashed into the new fingerprint at all — layout isn't identity, and hashing it would re-invalidate the world on every future layout change.
- Two extra bugs found while implementing: the filtered-session carry-through was copying legacy-format fingerprints under new-format keys (permanently unmatchable *and* un-grandfatherable — entries now stay under their own keys until visited), and the dry-run plan lacked the grandfather check, so its predictions would have disagreed with real runs.
- `TestDistillCacheGrandfathersLegacyEntries` proves the contract: a pre-upgrade cache — including a renamed-branch-dir session — costs **zero agent calls**, migrates to new keys, and a changed session still correctly re-distills. The ~14 hours of entire.io compute survives the upgrade.

**`docs/release-blockers.md`** is as explicit as the evidence allows. B1 (open) lays out the confound with a per-suite table quoting the exact leaked strings against the exact hidden validation they satisfy — e.g. the schema-contract suite's brain-arm prompt contains `"should rely on prompt plus local validation"` while a hidden check greps for that literal string in a test file, and both attribution suites hand the brain arm `"RealignAttributionBase newHead"` — the fix's exact call — plus the hidden test name. It states plainly that the audit's "without handing over hidden validation or expected text" sentence is false as written, that the numbers are real but the *attribution to the brain* is unsupported, why the leak auditor missed it (it scans transcripts, never `brain_queries` × hidden-validation overlap), and the four-step remediation required to clear it. R1–R4 are recorded as resolved with commits.

Meanwhile entire.io is at 2,393/2640 (4,192 facts) — final stretch. When it lands: the capstone four-arm eval plus the Gemma midtask read, and Phase 2 item 9 gets its verdict.

content.text:
While CI finishes (watching in the background), here's the full answer to both questions.

## Is it mergeable?

**Git-wise yes, CI almost.** After my cache-grandfathering commit, the `release-evidence` job correctly failed — the PR pins source hashes of `distill_cmd.go` into the distill-perf evidence manifest, and my changes made the retained artifacts stale. That's their evidence-integrity gate working exactly as designed, so I re-captured the evidence honestly rather than just bumping hashes: re-ran the manifest's exact recorded commands (deterministic local agent, `--force`, 256KB chunks) against a temp copy of the current brain on the current code. Result: **3.15× speedup** (jobs 1 → 4: 18.05s → 5.73s) versus the retained 2.0× claim — the cross-session pipeline that merged to main since the original capture lifts the measured number — with identical outputs on both arms (185 facts each, zero failures). Manifest, hashes, and audit reports regenerated; the full CI step reproduced locally end-to-end at exit 0; pushed as `b5e19a1`. The background watcher will confirm the live run.

**Review-wise: mergeable with one wording caveat.** All four code blockers are fixed and test-covered (R1–R4 in `docs/release-blockers.md`). The open item B1 — the benchmark confound — is a *claims* problem, not a code problem: nothing breaks at runtime, and the blockers doc now explicitly corrects the record inside the PR itself. My recommendation: **merge is defensible if B1 is treated as release-gating rather than merge-gating** — but note the inconsistency that `release_readiness_audit.md` still contains the sentence ("without handing over hidden validation or expected text") that `release-blockers.md` documents as false. The minimum-honesty merge would edit that one sentence and the two press-release "proof" bullets to point at B1. I left those edits to the author since they own the claims, but I can make them in two minutes if you'd rather merge clean.

## What I knowingly didn't fix (so: yes, open findings remain)

Two **majors** from the review, deliberately left because you scoped me to blockers:

1. **`distill --dry-run` predicts wrongly under the default `--agent auto`** — the dry-run path runs before agent resolution, so the cache salt hashes the literal string `"auto"` while real runs hash the resolved agent; predictions report cached sessions as to-distill. My grandfather wiring made first-run predictions accurate, but after migration (salted entries) the bug returns. Still zero dry-run tests.
2. **`brain status` runs uncapped fact verification** — hundreds of git subprocesses (`cat-file` + `for-each-ref --contains` per anchor, unmemoized) on a hot path, no opt-out.

Plus the ~15 documented minors (stderr cap failing successful chatty agents, distill evidence fields wiped by `facts review/promote/gc`, `--strict`/`--fail-on-unverifiable` sharing one bool, git-argv validation on anchor commits, Go-only symbol annotation in Radar, the stale 51-vs-52 and 1-suite-vs-3 audit numbers, the duplicated plan-doc line…).

And one finding the original review *didn't* catch but my own fresh evidence now demonstrates: the reviewer's "misleading metrics" point is visible in the recaptured artifacts — `extraction_seconds` reads 13.2s serial but 1.05s at jobs-4, because it measures consumer *wait* time, not work. Anyone citing it as "extraction took 1 second" would be misled; it should be renamed or summed across workers.

Want me to knock out the two majors (and the audit-sentence edit) before you merge, or merge now and fast-follow?

**`6acfb5a` — the two majors:**

content.text:
Here's the full remaining minor pile from the review, grouped — 15 items after subtracting the ones already fixed (the 51→52 count, the stale audit totals, and the press-release wording went in with `6acfb5a`):

**Distill pipeline polish (4):**
1. **stderr cap fails successful runs** — `distill_cmd.go` caps agent stderr at 256KB and errors on `Exceeded()` *even when the command exited 0*; worse, the cap check precedes the real-error check, so a failing *and* chatty agent reports "stderr exceeds N bytes" instead of its actual error. ~10 lines.
2. **Evidence fields wiped by facts admin** — `preserveFactDistillEvidence` keeps only 4 of ~15 new manifest fields; any `facts review/promote/gc` zeroes `Agent`, `Model`, `Jobs`, `TotalAgentCalls`, `TotalSeconds`, etc. — the fields the release audit reads. ~5 lines.
3. **Misleading metrics** — `extraction_seconds` measures consumer *wait*, not work (my own evidence recapture shows it: 13.2s serial vs 1.05s at jobs-4 for identical work), and `effective_extraction_jobs` is `min(requested, calls)`, not observed parallelism. Rename or fix semantics before anyone cites them.
4. **Dead code** — `distillChunkWork`'s unread fields, `distillPlan.Manifest`/`PrevCache` stored unused, `resolveDistillBranch` duplicating the `resolveBranch` closure (drift risk), and the `urlpkgParse` test seam no test uses.

**Verify/Radar correctness edges (4):**
5. **`--strict` and `--fail-on-unverifiable` bind the same bool** — `verify_cmd.go:121`; last flag silently wins, and the help texts describe different semantics. 
6. **Unvalidated git argv** — `verifyCommit` passes anchor-supplied commit strings straight into `git cat-file`/`for-each-ref`; a crafted anchor like `--upload-pack=…` lands as an argument. Local-only threat, but a `[0-9a-f]{4,64}` check matches the repo's hardening style. ~5 lines.
7. **Hinted Radar scan can silently drop the strongest signal** — when history names file hints and the hinted file is missing/skipped at load, no fallback scan runs and nothing is emitted, with no warning.
8. **Go-only symbol annotation** — `regressionFunctionPattern` matches only Go `func` decls while candidate files include ts/js/py/rs; `symbol` grouping silently degrades for non-Go code, undocumented. (Plus the tautological tail in `regressionNearbyCandidateSeenInSameSymbol` — works, but the dead condition obscures intent.)

**Smaller code nits (3):**
9. `mcpDebugToolName` is dead code; an unreachable re-check in `semantic_audit.go:~300`.
10. **Inconsistent path/redirect guards** — export write paths reject `"../"` but not bare `".."` (unlike `readBrainRelativeFile`), and the two Ollama-runner redirect policies differ (one silently stops, one errors) for the same condition.
11. **Silent provenance-hash degradation** — `fileSHA256Hex` returns `""` on read error, so `run_config.tasks_sha256` can be quietly absent; surfaces later as confusing eval-compare pairing notes rather than a warning at generation time.

**Docs/evidence hygiene (3):**
12. **MCP arg strictness is a breaking behavior change** — `additionalProperties: false` + validation now hard-errors on extra tool args that were previously ignored. Deliberate, but needs a release note for existing clients.
13. **Unverifiable precise numbers** — the audit quotes non-retained results to four decimal places (semantic refresh counts, the facts-smoke 42,124.75 tokens); hedged as non-proof, but either retain artifacts or round.
14. **Record-vs-log double-count** — in the radar-deletions evidence, every `mcp_history` record claims `mcp_tool_calls: 2` while the server log shows exactly one call; looks like client-side double-counting, the prompt mandates "EXACTLY ONCE", and the cross-checking auditor passes it. Doesn't change verdicts but dents the "auditor cross-checks everything" story.
15. **Duplicated line** — the `inspect boundaries` command appears twice in the PR's `semantic_brain_plan.md` edit (~lines 159/164).

My triage: items 1, 2, 5, and 6 are five-minute correctness fixes worth doing before merge (1 and 2 will bite real users; 5 and 6 are embarrassing-cheap). Item 3 matters if anyone ever cites the timing fields — rename now is cheapest. Item 12 just needs a sentence in the release notes. The rest are legitimate fast-follows or author's-choice cleanups. Want me to knock out 1/2/3/5/6 plus the release-note sentence in one commit?

132	// estimateTokens is a deterministic ~4-chars-per-token estimate over the text
133	// an agent would actually load (fact text plus its paths). It is a relative
134	// measure for comparing retrieval configurations, not an exact tokenizer.
135	func estimateTokens(facts []factRecord) int {
136		chars := 0
137		for _, f := range facts {
138			chars += len(f.Text) + len(strings.Join(f.Paths, ",")) + 4 // small per-fact framing
139		}
140		return (chars + 3) / 4
141	}
142	
143	func estimateRetrievedTokens(items []evalRetrievedItem) int {
144		chars := 0
145		for _, item := range items {
146			chars += len(item.Text) + len(item.Path) + 4
147		}
148		return (chars + 3) / 4
149	}

152	// of relevant fact ids. totalRelevant is the size of the labeled relevant set
153	// for recall; pass 0 when relevance came from a judge or source-match proxy
154	// labels (recall undefined).
155	func evalMetrics(surfaced []factRecord, relevant map[string]struct{}, totalRelevant int) evalTaskResult {
156		items := make([]evalRetrievedItem, len(surfaced))
157		for i, f := range surfaced {
158			items[i] = evalRetrievedItem{ID: f.ID, Text: f.Text, Path: strings.Join(f.Paths, ",")}
159		}
160		return evalItemMetrics(items, relevant, totalRelevant)
161	}
162	
163	func evalItemMetrics(surfaced []evalRetrievedItem, relevant map[string]struct{}, totalRelevant int) evalTaskResult {
164		res := evalTaskResult{Surfaced: len(surfaced), Tokens: estimateRetrievedTokens(surfaced)}
165		for _, item := range surfaced {
166			if _, ok := relevant[item.ID]; ok {
167				res.RelevantSurfaced++
168			}
169		}
170		if res.Surfaced > 0 {

172		}
173		if totalRelevant > 0 {
174			res.Recall = float64(res.RelevantSurfaced) / float64(totalRelevant)
175		}
176		if res.Tokens > 0 {
177			res.UsefulPer1k = float64(res.RelevantSurfaced) / (float64(res.Tokens) / 1000.0)
178		}
179		return res
180	}

1	# Semantic Brain Plan
2	
3	This plan describes how Entire Brain can grow from a session-history and seed
4	exporter into a modular agent-context system with semantic code intelligence,
5	impact analysis, branch-aware freshness, and multi-repo workspace support.
6	
7	The core constraint is that Entire Brain should remain the orchestration,
8	durable memory, and agent contract layer. Tree-sitter parsing and semantic
9	extraction should live behind a provider boundary, with `entire-sem` as the
10	expected provider.
11	
12	## Goals
13	
14	- Keep prior development history, seed context, and semantic code facts in one
15	  agent-readable brain.
16	- Make every generated artifact inspectable on disk.
17	- Separate historical rationale, current-code facts, and inferred impact.
18	- Support local development across many branches without treating one mutable
19	  snapshot as the whole truth.
20	- Scale to large repositories with incremental indexing and partial failure.
21	- Support multi-repo work through workspace brains layered over per-repo brains.
22	- Keep command-line and JSON contracts stable before adding additional
23	  transports.
24	
25	## Non-Goals
26	
27	- Do not make Entire Brain a monolithic parser.
28	- Do not require generated brain artifacts to be committed to the repository.
29	- Do not make embeddings mandatory for useful local behavior.
30	- Do not build browser or web UI surfaces as part of this plan.
31	
32	## Phase Boundary
33	
34	Phase 1 is local-only. It may read local repositories, local git history, local
35	Entire sessions, and locally installed provider output. It may run local tests in
36	CI. It must not publish generated brain artifacts, fetch generated brain
37	artifacts from remote services, send semantic content to hosted model APIs, or
38	expose a brain service over the network.
39	
40	Phase 1 commands must not perform implicit network operations. In particular:
41	
42	- `entire brain refresh index`, `refresh`, and `stale` must not run `git fetch`,
43	  `git pull`, or remote discovery; they may only inspect local refs.
44	- The semantic provider must run with no network egress during Phase 1 indexing.
45	- Local MCP means stdio transport only. The Phase 1 adapter must not open TCP or
46	  externally reachable Unix socket listeners, start network sidecars, perform
47	  auth callbacks, upload telemetry, or call hosted models.
48	
49	The following features are Phase 3 unless explicitly implemented with a
50	local-only backend:
51	
52	- Publishing or hydrating shared brain baselines.
53	- CI uploading generated brain artifacts for reuse.
54	- Remote embeddings or any embedding provider that receives source, symbols,
55	  docs, summaries, or semantic records.
56	- Hosted-model semantic summaries, seed enrichments, architecture summaries,
57	  risk summaries, or wiki-like generated docs.
58	- Remote MCP, HTTP, or daemon serving of brain data beyond local stdio/localhost
59	  development.
60	- Telemetry or metrics upload.
61	- Remote artifact registries or baseline discovery services.
62	- Cross-machine workspace membership sync.
63	- Remote repo fetch/index-by-URL flows that clone or fetch code as part of brain
64	  generation.
65	- Cloud review or eval integrations that package semantic context for external
66	  agents.
67	
68	Local filesystem bundle import/export is allowed in Phase 1 when both source and
69	destination are explicit local paths. It must not contact a registry, object
70	store, remote URL, CI artifact service, or discovery service.
71	
72	## System Shape
73	
74	The system should be layered.
75	
76	### Entire Brain
77	
78	Owns:
79	
80	- Brain directory layout.
81	- Manifest format.
82	- Session export.
83	- Seed export.
84	- Refresh policy.
85	- Staleness checks.
86	- Agent-facing intake templates.
87	- Query, context, impact, and review commands.
88	- Workspace coordination.
89	
90	### Semantic Provider
91	
92	`entire-sem` should own:
93	
94	- Tree-sitter parsing.
95	- Entity extraction.
96	- Language-specific symbol models.
97	- Semantic diffs.
98	- Import, call, inheritance, field access, route, and tool relation extraction.
99	- Parser capability reporting.
100	- Partial failure reporting.
101	
102	Entire Brain should shell out to the provider or consume provider artifacts
103	through a stable JSON contract. It should not import provider internals.
104	
105	### Semantic Store
106	
107	A new storage/query layer should ingest provider artifacts and expose:
108	
109	- Symbol search.
110	- Relation traversal.
111	- Impact analysis.
112	- Changed-symbol reports.
113	- Route/tool/workflow maps.
114	- Staleness metadata.
115	
116	The first implementation can use JSONL plus SQLite. The rest of the code should
117	depend on a narrow interface so the backing store can evolve.
118	
119	### Agent Surface
120	
121	Agents should use a small command set first. `brief` is the front door for
122	coding agents; specialist semantic and history tools live under `inspect` so
123	agents do not have to choose from a wide top-level command surface.
124	
125	```sh
126	entire brain status [repo] --json
127	entire brain brief "<task>" --json
128	entire brain search "<query>" --json
129	entire brain show <id> --json
130	entire brain refresh [repo] --json
131	entire brain guide
132	entire brain path [repo]
133	```
134	
135	The normal agent loop should start with one command:
136	
137	```sh
138	entire brain brief "<task>" --json
139	```
140	
141	`brief` should combine brain freshness, semantic code facts, seeded baseline
142	context, history-derived decisions, likely files, likely tests, known pitfalls,
143	provenance, and a cheap live-state overlay into one bounded packet. The
144	live-state overlay should include branch, HEAD, dirty file list, staged vs
145	unstaged state, diff stats, and changed-symbol hints when available. It must
146	make clear that the brain is an indexed snapshot and may not include edits the
147	same agent made minutes ago. Agents should inspect full diffs or file contents
148	only when the task intersects those live changes or when `brief` returns low
149	confidence.
150	
151	Specialist/debug surfaces should move under `inspect`:
152	
153	```sh
154	entire brain inspect code "<query>" --json
155	entire brain inspect context <symbol-or-id> --json
156	entire brain inspect impact <symbol-or-file> --json
157	entire brain inspect changes --base main --head HEAD --json
158	entire brain inspect tests "<query>" --json
159	entire brain inspect boundaries --kind route|tool|workflow --json
160	entire brain inspect regressions "<query>" --json
161	entire brain search "<query>" --json
162	entire brain query "<query>" --json
163	entire brain get <result-id> --json
164	```
165	
166	Workspace use has its own front door:
167	
168	```sh
169	entire brain workspace query <name> "<symbol-or-query>" --json
170	entire brain workspace impact <name> "<symbol-or-query>" --json
171	entire brain workspace refresh <name> --json
172	```
173	
174	Each command should provide concise human output and a stable `--json` mode.
175	
176	## Semantic Artifact Contract
177	
178	Define a versioned JSON schema emitted by the semantic provider and consumed by
179	Entire Brain. The provider is an artifact emitter: it parses source and emits
180	versioned semantic facts. Entire Brain owns persistence, indexing, query
181	behavior, freshness policy, and agent presentation.
182	
183	Initial provider commands:
184	
185	```sh
186	entire sem snapshot --repo . --format ndjson
187	entire sem symbols --repo . --format ndjson
188	entire sem edges --repo . --format ndjson
189	entire sem diff --base main --head HEAD --json
190	entire sem doctor --json
191	```
192	
193	Provider output should support newline-delimited JSON from the first release.
194	Large repositories can produce hundreds of megabytes of semantic facts, so a
195	single whole-repo JSON document should be a compatibility/debug mode, not the
196	primary integration format.
197	
198	Initial snapshot header:
199	
200	```json
201	{
202	  "schema_version": "1.0",
203	  "repo_root": "/path/to/repo",
204	  "commit": "abc123",
205	  "tree": "tree789",
206	  "languages": ["Go", "Python"],

2	
3	## Status addendum (2026-06-10)
4	
5	The per-phase "current status" notes below are dated ~2026-06-01 and predate the
6	most recent harness work. Current state:
7	
8	- **Phase 1 (repeatable harness) and Phase 2 (discovery): done.** 39 task

14	  tasks × 4 repetitions. Welch t-test + Holm–Bonferroni significance is
15	  implemented (commits fb7ca3f, 2a4c4fe). A `prep` subcommand (cd547d5)
16	  validates brain caches without agent runs.
17	- **Phase 4 (demo evidence): not started.**
18	- **Reconciling panel size vs. layer targets:** Phase 2's "20+ significant
19	  scenarios per layer" is the *discovery* goal; the 8-task panel is the
20	  *committed proof subset* for reproducible Phase 3 runs. The panel grows as
21	  discovery retains more brain-positive scenarios; the two numbers are not in
22	  conflict.
23	- **Known open items:** real SWE-bench Lite/Verified integration (Layer C),
24	  the cross-repo workspace task (declared not-runnable in the panel), Codex
25	  model attribution (pinned via flag but not echoed in output), and expanding
26	  full-brain (checkpoint-history) tasks in the panel.
27	
28	## Summary
29	
30	This benchmark measures whether Codex and Claude Code perform better on real
31	repository tasks when they can use Entire Brain.
32	
33	The first version should optimize for a repeatable harness, then use the same
34	run artifacts to produce demo-quality before/after evidence. The benchmark
35	starts with three local repositories. The checked-in task fixtures use portable
36	repo names; runners resolve them from the benchmark workspace or explicit task
37	paths:
38	
39	- `entire-brain`
40	- `entire-cli`
41	- GitHub CLI
42	
43	The benchmark should compare agent performance across controlled context
44	conditions, not just tool latency. Useful outcomes include faster localization,
45	better test selection, fewer irrelevant file reads, fewer wrong edits, and
46	better recovery of implementation rationale.
47	
48	The Phase 2 benchmark should optimize across three scenario layers:
49	
50	- Layer A: project-native hard tasks in the two repositories with Entire session
51	  data: `entire-brain` and `entire-cli`.
52	- Layer B: project-native hard tasks in GitHub CLI.
53	- Layer C: SWE-bench-style tasks with issue prompts, hidden tests, fixed base
54	  commits, and no repo-specific hints beyond the condition policy.
55	
56	The model, reasoning-effort, turn, token, duration, and cost matrix is not a
57	separate Phase 2 layer. It is a later overlay applied to retained scenarios in
58	Layers A, B, and C.
59	
60	## Context Conditions
61	
62	Run each task under these conditions when the repo supports them:
63	
64	1. **No brain**
65	   - The agent receives the task prompt and normal repository access.
66	   - The agent must not run `entire brain ...`.
67	   - No brain docs or MCP tools are preloaded.
68	   - Codex and Claude still use their host auth state, but the harness disables
69	     persistent sessions, user config/rules, slash commands, and MCP config.
70	
71	2. **Semantic brain only**
72	   - The agent receives the task prompt plus Entire Brain semantic intake
73	     instructions.
74	   - The harness prepares seed and semantic artifacts with local-only commands.
75	   - The agent may use `stale`, `query`, `context`, `impact`, `changes`,
76	     `routes`, `tools`, `workflows`, `tests`, and workspace commands.
77	   - Checkpoint transcript/session history is withheld.
78	
79	3. **Full brain**
80	   - Includes semantic brain plus exported Entire checkpoint history.
81	   - The agent may use seed context, semantic facts, history gaps, checkpoint
82	     metadata, prompts, and transcripts.
83	   - This full-history form is available for `entire-brain` and `entire-cli`.
84	   - For GitHub CLI, which has no Entire checkpoint history, the full-brain
85	     condition means the complete available brain package for that repo
86	     (`history_available=false`); do not report GitHub CLI wins as
87	     full-history wins.
88	
89	Keep the base task prompt identical across conditions. Only the allowed context
90	policy changes.
91	
92	For stale-context tasks, prepare the brain first, then apply and commit the
93	regression. These tasks measure whether the agent treats prepared context as a
94	cache with a freshness contract rather than as ground truth.
95	
96	## Checkpoint Availability
97	
98	Checkpoint history is materially different across the starting repos.
99	
100	| Repo | Checkpoint source | Checkpoints | Session metadata | Prompts | Transcripts |
101	|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
102	| `entire-brain` | local `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1` | 30 | 142 | 142 | 142 |
103	| `entire-cli` | `https://github.com/entireio/cli-checkpoints.git`, `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1` | 3,945 | 5,426 | 4,656 | 5,088 |
104	| GitHub CLI | none found locally/configured | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
105	
106	The `entire-cli` checkout stores checkpoint discovery in
107	`.entire/settings.json`:
108	
109	```json
110	{
111	  "strategy_options": {
112	    "checkpoint_remote": {
113	      "provider": "github",
114	      "repo": "entireio/cli-checkpoints"
115	    }
116	  }
117	}
118	```
119	
120	Entire Brain export discovers checkpoints by trying local refs first, then
121	falling back to the configured checkpoint remote and fetching only the v1
122	checkpoint ref into a temporary repository. Ignore v2 checkpoints for this
123	benchmark.
124	
125	## Harness
126	
127	Add a benchmark harness under `benchmarks/agent-brain/`:
128	
129	- `tasks/*.yaml` defines repo, base commit, prompt, context condition, timeout,
130	  expected files, validation commands, and scoring checks.
131	- `adapters/codex.*` and `adapters/claude.*` run the agents in disposable
132	  worktrees.
133	- `brain/prepare.*` builds isolated brain state in temporary plugin dirs.
134	- `runs/<timestamp>/...` stores prompts, transcripts, commands, diffs, test
135	  output, timing, and scoring data.
136	- `score.*` calculates deterministic scores from tests, patches, touched files,
137	  and rubric checks.
138	
139	Use fixed base commits and clean disposable worktrees. Avoid mutating the source
140	checkouts during benchmark runs.
141	
142	## Initial Scenarios
143	
144	Start with nine tasks: three per repository.
145	
146	### `entire-brain`
147	
148	1. **Semantic command bugfix**
149	   - Fix a narrow issue in `stale`, `query`, or `context`.
150	   - Brain benefit: semantic commands should identify the relevant functions and
151	     tests quickly.
152	   - Validate with focused semantic tests and `go test ./...`.
153	
154	2. **MCP and CLI contract change**
155	   - Add or adjust one semantic JSON field while keeping MCP wrappers compatible.
156	   - Brain benefit: `impact` should reveal the CLI command, JSON output path,
157	     MCP adapter, and contract tests.
158	   - Validate with semantic and MCP tests.
159	
160	3. **Workspace behavior task**
161	   - Change workspace query or impact behavior in a bounded way.
162	   - Brain benefit: workspace context should locate freshness handling and
163	     workspace tests.
164	   - Validate with workspace tests.
165	
166	### `entire-cli`
167	
168	1. **Agent integration fix**
169	   - Fix a Codex or Claude hook/session edge case.
170	   - Brain benefit: full brain should recover prior rationale and point to
171	     agent integration surfaces.
172	   - Validate with focused unit/integration tests.
173	
174	2. **External command/plugin behavior**
175	   - Adjust plugin dispatch, external command behavior, or env filtering.
176	   - Brain benefit: semantic context should connect dispatch code, plugin code,
177	     and integration tests.
178	   - Validate with external command/plugin tests.
179	
180	3. **Review/resume context task**

{"author":"suhaanthayyil","branch":"claude/layer-b-scenarios","mergeable":"MERGEABLE","size":"+1971/-1 in 16 files","title":"Seed Layer-B github-cli benchmark scenarios + committed discovery ledger"}
---body---
## Summary

Layer B of the Phase-2 benchmark (project-native GitHub CLI tasks, no Entire session history — proves seed+semantic value only) was at **zero** candidate scenarios. This PR seeds it properly:

- **5 new task definitions**, each mechanically verified at the pinned `base_commit` (`da68cb8f`, cli/cli upstream main 2026-06-08): clean test PASS → injection applied (old string matches exactly once) → focused hidden test FAIL → package still builds → revert → PASS.
  - `ghrepo-url-git-suffix` — shared remote-URL parser drops `.git` trimming (architecture-localization)
  - `display-url-scheme` — shared URL display helper forces https (architecture-localization)
  - `tenant-name-dot` — tenant-host detection loses the `.`-prefix rationale (rationale-recovery)
  - `search-quote-multiword` — shared search-query serializer stops quoting spaces (architecture-localization)
  - `pr-checks-summary` — shared PR-checks summary loses its all-failing special case (validation-selection)
- **5 existing github-cli tasks upgraded to release-grade**: pinned `base_commit`, declared `archetype`, explicit `leak_markers` canaries (release-panel preflight requires them with hidden validation).
- **Honest ledger counting**: `generate_layer_b_scenarios` now emits **one ledger row per task** when the task declares its archetype (the Phase-2 counting rule: a scenario = one unique task shape). The old task×archetype cross-join inflated counts and truncated coverage at `--minimum-per-layer` after ~4 tasks. Unknown archetypes fail loudly; tasks without the field keep the legacy cross-join. 4 new tests cover this.
- **Committed discovery ledger** `discovery/phase2-layer-b-20260610/`: Layer B = 10 one-per-task rows with hypothesis, expected brain source, primary metric, and recommended repetitions (pilot 1 / proof minimum 4).

## What this does NOT claim

These are **candidates, not proofs**. No agent benchmark runs were performed; `candidate_goal_met` stays `false` (10 < 21). No-brain pilots and repeated proof runs are the next step. One shape note: `ghrepo-url-git-suffix` is adjacent to the existing `repo-name-trims-dotgit` (both involve `.git` suffixes) but targets a different parser at a different layer with a different symptom (remote-URL resolution 404s vs argument normalization) — flagged here so reviewers can judge.

## Leakage controls

All 10 tasks: both hide flags set; prompts are symptom-only (audited: no file paths, function names, test names, fix text, or brain_query identifiers in any prompt); `brain_queries` reach brain conditions only; explicit `leak_markers` make output leak-audits precise.

## Verification

- `run.py check --tasks 'github-cli-*'` → exit 0, 10/10 `fails-as-expected` (run on this exact branch lineage)
- `python3 -m unittest run_test` → 152 tests OK on this lineage
- `mise run check` and `mise run release:evidence` → pass (no Go changes; retained proofs untouched)

Stacked on #33 (same evidence-gate machinery); retarget to `main` after #33 merges.

import json, glob, re
# B1 lens: for each task, intersect brain_queries terms with (a) hidden

for f in sorted(glob.glob("benchmarks/agent-brain/tasks/github-cli-*.json")):
    d=json.load(open(f))
    name=f.split("/")[-1].replace("github-cli-","").replace(".json","")
    bq=" ".join(d.get("brain_queries",[]))
    hv=json.dumps(d.get("hidden_validation",""))+json.dumps(d.get("validation",""))
    inj=json.dumps(d.get("inject",d.get("injection","")))
    # tokens >=4 chars from brain_queries that appear in hidden validation or injection
    toks=set(t for t in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]{3,}", bq))
    leak_hv=sorted(t for t in toks if t in hv)
    leak_inj=sorted(t for t in toks if t in inj and t not in ("github","string"))
    print(f"{name:28s} bq_terms={len(toks):2d} in_hidden_validation={leak_hv[:4]} in_injection={leak_inj[:4]}")
EOF

Review complete. **The work is solid — but every one of the ten tasks ships with the exact B1 confound, freshly authored.** Here's the full picture.

## What checks out

- **The mechanical verification claim is real.** I cloned `cli/cli` at the pinned `da68cb8f` and ran the full cycle on a sampled task: hidden test PASSES clean → injection's old-string matches exactly once → hidden test FAILS → package still builds → revert → PASSES. Exactly as documented.
- **The generator fix is correct and well-tested**: declared archetype → one ledger row, unknown archetype errors loudly, undeclared tasks keep the legacy cross-join (old ledgers stay reproducible), and the `--minimum-per-layer` truncation behavior is pinned by one of the 4 new tests. All 152 harness tests pass.
- **The ledger is honest**: Layer B = 10 one-per-task rows, `candidate_goal_met: false` (10 < 21), no proof claims anywhere, and the author self-flagged the `.git`-suffix task adjacency.
- **Base prompts are genuinely symptom-only** — I checked; no paths, function names, or fix text.
- CI is green after I retargeted the PR from the merged `codex/release-readiness-hardening` branch to `main`; merge state is CLEAN.

## The finding

I intersected each task's `brain_queries` against its hidden validation: **all ten tasks hand the brain arm the exact function name the hidden test exercises** — `PrCheckStatusSummaryWithColor`, `StandardSearchString`, `NormalizeRepoName`, `TenantName`, `FromURL`, `AddJSONFlags`, `AddFormatFlags`, `CheckAuth`, `ScopesSuggestion`, `DisplayURL`. For tasks whose declared archetype is literally *architecture-localization* — where the measured skill is finding that function from symptoms — the query terms are the answer key. The harness injects `brain_queries` into brain-arm prompts only, so this is B1's hint asymmetry reproduced in new tasks, on the same branch lineage where `docs/release-blockers.md` documents it. The PR's leakage section says "audited: no … brain_query identifiers in any prompt" — true of the *base* prompt, but it's the same blind spot the #33 auditor had: nobody audits what the harness injects.

Because the PR explicitly claims candidates-not-proofs, this isn't a merge-blocker by the B1 framing — but merging as-is bakes confounded queries into ten tasks that will need rework before any pilot can graduate, and the discovery pilots themselves would measure hint+brain.

## My recommendation

Fix before merge — it's cheap and surgical: replace the identifier terms with symptom-level query terms derived from each prompt (e.g. `"pr checks summary all failing"` instead of `PrCheckStatusSummaryWithColor`), which still serves the design intent (realistic queries an agent would form from the symptom) without handing over the localization answer. Optionally also land B1's leak-auditor extension (brain_queries × hidden-validation intersection — my review check is essentially the implementation) so this becomes self-enforcing instead of review-dependent.

Want me to make both fixes on the branch and merge, or hand the finding back to suhaanthayyil?
